title: All-skills configuration and production assurance: consolidated four-stage deep research

tldr.content: Final decision: do not add a transparent universal config merge. Add a constrained, host-owned configuration boundary with one closed versioned envelope, independently registered per-skill schemas, field-specific merge rules, immutable effective snapshots, and exact provenance. Keep authority, security invariants, credentials, lifecycle, evaluator gates, and publication control outside ordinary config. csm-orchestrate remains a fail-closed prototype until the assurance gates below are proven.

executiveSummary.content:
This report combines the prior three-pass csm-orchestrate approach/fault/limitation research with a new three-pass DEEP configuration study. The first configuration pass inventoried defaults and proposed a JSON envelope; the second challenged its security, coverage, migration, and merge semantics; the third adversarially rejected a uniform policy plane and finalized a narrower host-owned design.

original grill approach + shipped controller -> prior three-pass audit -> config inventory/design -> config challenge -> final adversarial assurance

The repository currently has 14 skills with incompatible ownership, state, artifact, side-effect, and configuration models. A common transport/provenance envelope is useful; a common semantic configuration object is unsafe. Production grade requires a trust protocol, not merely JSON Schema: authenticated delegation, exact request-bound approvals, immutable artifact snapshots, independent signal appraisal, linearizable state/history, explicit unknown states, executable remediation limits, telemetry, held-out evaluation, and rollback.

keyFindings.content:
K1. supported: d2fd905 substantially implements the grill approach's structural controller: canonical JSON phases, capability metadata, typed handoffs, bounded local scheduling, gates, schema migration, retry intent, and receipt lineage [R1][R2].
K2. partially-supported: Requirement/signal IDs are structural binding only; they are not semantic evidence entailment without an independent validator over exact artifact bytes/snapshot [R3][R4].
K3. partially-supported: Host-backed review is fail-closed against local callbacks, but in-process markers and host-returned fields do not prove host authentication, reviewer isolation, or reviewer correctness [R5][R6].
K4. not-supported: Cross-process ownership, exactly-once arbitrary effects, and completed cancellation are absent from process-local queues/maps and AbortSignals [R7][R8].
K5. not-supported: Activation predicates are not evaluated, remediation budgets are not consumed, and insertedAfter is metadata-only rather than executable ordering [R1].
K6. supported: A configuration transport envelope plus per-skill schemas is the safest common layer; a uniform merge/API is not [R9][R10].
K7. supported: Config must be parsed strictly, resolved from a trusted snapshot, field-authorized, patched through a restricted profile, canonicalized, digested, provenance-recorded, and reauthorized at the final sink [R9][R11][R12].
K8. supported: No-config behavior must remain unchanged and skills must migrate one at a time through explicit adapters; csm-upload, csm-browse, csm-autoresearch, and csm-build require host/security treatment before ordinary preferences are exposed [R13].
K9. supported: Production grade requires G0 contract safety through G8 autonomy gates, including durable CAS/fencing/history, independent semantic validation, telemetry completeness, held-out adjudication, shadow/canary control, and tested rollback [R14][R15][R16].
K10. supported: The defensible runtime guarantee is at-least-once execution with durable reconciliation and sink-side idempotency where possible, not exactly-once arbitrary external effects [R7][R8].

detailSections.content:
Approach differences and existing faults: the controller matches canonical JSON authority, producer ownership, route foundations, typed child lineage, separate technical/functional gates, bounded local scheduling, schema migration, retry intent, status projection, and durable receipt interfaces. It differs from the grill approach because activation predicates remain descriptive heuristics, phase-level adversarial review can be local, remediation budgets are metadata rather than consumed counters, inserted phases are appended, ordinary approvals do not bind the complete request/input set, process-local state is not distributed coordination, and tests are synthetic rather than production evidence.

Configuration inventory: classify each value before exposing it. Immutable safety invariants include schema IDs/revisions, run/artifact identity, ownership/lineage, terminal transitions, hard ceilings, no-symlink/path policy, credential isolation, network/browser separation, evaluator hard gates, bootstrap identity, trust roots, and publication confirmation. Host policy ceilings include maximum time, memory, processes, output, retries, concurrency, network/browser scope, and destinations. Skill-owned behavior includes lifecycle, evaluator semantics, artifact format, renderer policy, and side-effect classification. User preferences include bounded verbosity, selected read-only dimensions, viewport, report presentation, and other non-authority choices. Fixtures include fake ports, timestamps, hashes, and test-only values.

The 14-skill migration surface: csm-autoresearch (sandbox/evaluator/resource policy), csm-bdd-tdd (plan/spec package), csm-browse (container/image/ports/cookies), csm-build (write/execute/commit authority), csm-ddd (bounded analysis), csm-deep-research (source mode/tier and research-only writes), csm-grill (approach content), csm-make-tests (test generation and writes), csm-plan (planning inputs/applicability), csm-review (review posture/evidence), csm-review-python (tool pins/doctrine), csm-scan (limits/dimensions and NORMS write inconsistency), csm-upload (legacy config/publication/credentials), and csm-orchestrate (host policy/route limits). Shared libraries own parsing, canonicalization, validation, redaction, and typed errors; they do not own authorization.

Prescribed config envelope (illustrative JSON):
{
  "schema": "csm-skill-config-envelope/1",
  "configId": "config-example",
  "subject": {"skill": "csm-plan", "skillDigest": "sha256:...", "owner": "operator", "runId": "run-..."},
  "skillConfigSchema": {"id": "csm-plan-config/1", "revision": 1, "digest": "sha256:..."},
  "baseConfigDigest": "sha256:...",
  "layers": [{"source": "repository-file", "path": ".agents/config/csm-plan.json", "fileDigest": "sha256:..."}],
  "patches": [{"patchId": "patch-example", "baseDigest": "sha256:...", "operations": [{"op": "test", "path": "/limits/maxBytes", "value": 1000000}, {"op": "replace", "path": "/limits/maxBytes", "value": 500000}]}],
  "effectiveConfigDigest": "sha256:...",
  "canonicalization": "repository-canonical-json/1",
  "policyDigest": "sha256:...",
  "issuedAt": "2026-08-27T00:00:00Z",
  "expiresAt": "2026-08-27T01:00:00Z",
  "nonce": "nonce-example"
}

The envelope is transport/provenance, not semantic authority. Each skill has a registered closed `csm-<skill>-config/1` schema and adapter. Precedence is host hard ceiling -> signed deployment policy -> authenticated operator policy -> repository/run data where allowed -> explicit user preference. “Explicit” is not automatically higher trust. Lower-trust layers may only narrow limits, permissions, destinations, and scopes; preferences use documented replace semantics; ambiguous or widening conflicts reject. JSON Patch is restricted to `test`, `replace`, and narrow `add`; reject root replacement, remove, move, copy, unknown members, protected pointers, excessive depth/size, and unauthorized paths. Validate the final effective object plus semantic policy, compute the digest, and bind it to approval/invocation/cursor/receipt/audit/final sink. No environment interpolation, URLs, dynamic schema loading, plugins, raw secrets, or config-controlled authority in version 1.

Production assurance protocol: canonicalize request R; sign an audience-bound one-time approval over request/config/input/graph/policy/validator/reviewer/output digests and attempt; atomically consume it while creating a fenced dispatch intent; resolve immutable content-addressed input snapshots; independently run registered signal validators and reviewer; authenticate and validate host/reviewer/artifact attestations; commit monotonic terminal history; treat timeout/cancellation as UNKNOWN until reconciled. A durable store needs CAS, fencing, unique idempotency records, atomic intent/terminal writes, append-only history, and late-result handling. External effects remain at-least-once unless the sink supplies idempotency or transactionality.

Operational gates: instrument every parent/phase/edge/child/attempt/approval/retry/review/resolver/cursor/terminal event; use traces for causal context and metrics for aggregate SLIs. Build visible, validation, held-out, and post-deployment corpora; use blinded independent adjudication and confidence intervals. Run deterministic/fault-injection tests, shadow mode, synthetic external systems, then an isolated contemporaneous-control canary. Stop on any critical false VERIFIED, unauthorized effect, duplicate non-idempotent effect, stale fence, provenance mismatch, unreconciled timeout/cancellation, missing audit/telemetry, control contamination, or rollback failure.

recommendation.content: Adopt configuration as an opt-in, host-owned boundary, not a global transparent default. First freeze and inventory no-config behavior and classify every default. Then implement the envelope, registry, strict parser, secure snapshot loader, restricted patch profile, field policy/merge algebra, effective digest/provenance, and per-skill adapters. Migrate one low-risk read-only preference first; keep csm-upload's legacy config separate and migrate it last. Do not expose browser credentials, evaluator policy, publication authority, commit/execute capability, trust roots, or hard safety ceilings to ordinary config. Keep csm-orchestrate production autonomy disabled until G0-G8 pass repeatedly in deployment-like conditions.

unverifiedClaims.content: Unknown: whether the real host authenticates its identity and reviewer, whether attestations use trusted keys and correct audiences, whether approvals are atomically consumed and revoked, whether artifact resolution returns immutable bytes, whether the cursor store is linearizable across processes, whether timeout/cancellation late effects can be reconciled, whether sink-side idempotency exists, whether signal validators are correct and isolated, whether configuration source ownership and file permissions are enforceable, whether all 14 no-config behaviors can remain equivalent, whether the workload corpus and adjudicators are representative, and whether any measured improvement is causal. JSON Schema defaults/format, hashes, signatures, trace presence, green CI, and inter-rater agreement do not prove these claims.

references.content: Local claims are pinned to commit d2fd905 and the repository's current source/schema/test surfaces. External authority was retrieved 2026-08-27: JSON Schema 2020-12; RFC 6901/6902/7396/8259/8785/9700; XDG Base Directory; OWASP input validation, secrets, SSRF, and AI-agent guidance; CWE-20/22/73/345/367/441; NIST SP 800-53, SP 800-63-4, AI RMF Measure; RATS; SLSA; Temporal; Cloudflare Workflows; etcd; OpenTelemetry; Google SRE; Cochrane.

processAppendix.content: This consolidated finding incorporates the earlier three-pass csm-orchestrate report and a new three-pass configuration study. New pass 1 used four independent tracks for defaults inventory, JSON contract design, config security, and migration. New pass 2 used four independent challengers for schema/merge, coverage, security, and migration. New pass 3 used four adversarial tracks for config architecture, security, migration, and production readiness. The final synthesis corrected overclaims, separated data from authority, narrowed the universal-config proposal, and produced the minimum sufficient protocol and rollout gates. All research agents were instructed read-only; one earlier delegated config researcher unexpectedly wrote an auxiliary Markdown finding, which remains disclosed and was not silently removed. No implementation code was changed in this research run.

claims.statement: The shipped csm-orchestrate implementation is substantially faithful to the original grill approach structurally, but remains a fail-closed controller prototype rather than a production-complete outer loop.
Requirement and acceptance-signal IDs create structural binding but do not establish semantic entailment without an independently trusted validator over an immutable snapshot.
Process-local queues and maps cannot provide cross-process ownership, exactly-once arbitrary effects, or completed cancellation after timeout.
Activation predicates, remediation budget consumption, and physical insertion ordering remain functional gaps against the grill approach.
A closed versioned configuration envelope plus independently registered per-skill schemas is a viable common transport layer, but a uniform semantic config object is unsafe across the 14 skills.
JSON Patch may be used only as a restricted, base-digest-checked, field-authorized transformation; RFC 6902 alone is not an authorization policy language.

Effective configuration must be securely parsed, snapshot-resolved, semantically authorized, canonicalized, digested, provenance-recorded, and reauthorized at the final effect sink; schema validity and hashes alone are insufficient.

No-config compatibility and one-skill-at-a-time adapters are required because csm-upload, csm-browse, csm-autoresearch, csm-build, csm-scan, and the analysis/review skills have materially different authorities and side effects.
Production autonomy requires contract, configuration, authorization, durable execution, semantic acceptance, observability, held-out evaluation, and shadow/canary rollback gates before enablement.
The strongest honest runtime guarantee is at-least-once execution with durable reconciliation, fencing, and sink-side idempotency where available, not exactly-once arbitrary external effects.
